authority.scope: Review current S41 code for signed venue readers, selected DPAPI/native configuration, error/repr/report leakage, provider/Discovery authority, holdout and capital boundaries, and V1 regression surface.
limitations: This is source inspection only. It does not establish behavior of the pinned third-party venue adapters, runtime host qualification, or live exchange/provider security.
No tests were run. XML/JUnit and historical checkpoint results were not used as proof of the source findings below.
The S41 worktree has no final integration SHA; reviewed HEAD is dirty and the cited files may differ in the final integrated tree.

findings.title: Signed venue reads inherit ambient proxy configuration

evidence.observation: The production default opener is `urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirect)`; it does not install an empty ProxyHandler or otherwise disable proxy discovery.
The Binance reader uses the same opener pattern while retaining the selected credential and signing requests.
The selected demo child filters credential-named environment variables but passes other environment variables, including HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY, through to the reader process.

findings.impact: Python's default urllib opener includes ProxyHandler, which consults ambient proxy configuration. HTTPS certificate validation prevents an ordinary CONNECT proxy from reading request headers, but a configured TLS-inspecting proxy trusted by the host can observe the API key header and signed request. The code does not make that proxy trust decision explicit.
findings.recommended_resolution: Disable ambient proxies for these signed venue readers with an explicit empty ProxyHandler, or add a reviewed owner-configured trusted proxy policy. Keep venue hosts fixed and preserve normal TLS verification.
findings.evidence_limit: No credentials were used and no request was sent; this is a source-level exposure path, not an observed credential leak.

findings.title: Demo reader error and receipt boundaries redact credentials and server text

evidence.observation: The reader uses generic fixed error codes, rejects redirects/unexpected endpoint identity, discards exception text, and rejects receipts containing the API key or secret.
DemoCredential suppresses values in repr; response failures use fixed codes and exception details are discarded; credentials are checked against canonical response content.

Persisted/displayed selected-demo status contains config/venue/environment/profile, a profile status and reason codes, and explicit false capital/assisted flags; it does not serialize credential values.

GUI and component errors report exception type only; child stdout/stderr are discarded. The credential entry UI uses password mode, emits a fixed success/failure message, and clears local variables in finally blocks.

caveats: Python strings cannot be reliably zeroized; clearing local names is best-effort lifetime reduction, not memory erasure.

The native Nautilus config is constructed with credentials at `src/atlas/runtime/bybit_demo.py:68-96` and `src/atlas/runtime/binance_demo.py:110-133`; this review found no application serialization/logging of those config objects, but did not audit the pinned third-party SDK's internal logging or object repr.

findings.title: Selected secrets use current-user DPAPI and are separated from public runtime

evidence.observation: The secret store uses Windows DPAPI with UI disabled, has no plaintext/non-Windows fallback, binds demo credentials to opaque reference/venue/environment, bounds ciphertext/plaintext, and converts malformed bindings to generic errors.
The selected demo and public ops children inherit a filtered environment and send stdout/stderr to DEVNULL. The public launch does not carry credential-named environment values.
Only the critic broker retrieves the provider key; it is started as a separate owner-checked process with a DPAPI-protected context and filtered environment.

caveats: The GUI accepts keys as Python strings before DPAPI protection; those strings are cleared by reassignment but cannot be guaranteed erased from process memory.
This code review does not establish Windows ACLs, OS account isolation, or credential behavior inside Nautilus.

findings.title: Discovery read scope, provider dispatch, and final holdout checks are bounded in the host

evidence.observation: Requests must bind an untouched preregistered Discovery family, exact allowed refs/cutoffs and remaining budgets. Read access filters artifact types, future evidence, prohibited holdout/outcome material, and attempt metadata linked to the final holdout.

The one-shot worker clears its environment, unshares namespaces, receives only bounded request/evidence bytes and a broker socket, and emits a fixed generic failure message. It has no network namespace access or mounted run database.

Provider endpoints/models are fixed, no hosted tools are configured, provider HTTP clients disable ambient environment trust, prompts are bounded, and raw SDK failure text is normalized. `build_user_prompt` omits inaccessible holdout identities.
HMAC capabilities bind durable authorizations, fixed provider/model/endpoints and call/token ceilings; critic capabilities bind one call and zero dynamic tools. Broker failures become fixed codes.
The critic profile fixes DeepSeek task identity, endpoint, call/token limits and dynamic_tools=0. Event extraction has typed bounded request/output contracts.
Critic receipts are rejected unless source receipts declare disabled agent mode and capital/assisted false; recorded results remain shadow evidence.

findings.holdout_disclosure_note: The internal ResearchProposalRequest carries inaccessible holdout identity hashes through the worker/broker contract for host-side authorization and validation (`contracts.py:392,464-475`); the external proposer prompt is manually constructed and does not include those identities (`provider.py:72-99`). No holdout labels, scores, returns, or outcome artifacts were found in the readable evidence surface.
findings.authority_note: No path was found by which Discovery or action-critic output changes selection, risk, admission, an order, protection, recovery, or capital authority. This is code inspection, not a proof of end-to-end runtime isolation.

findings.title: Selected native demo OMS keeps opening authority closed and reports capital disabled

evidence.observation: Credential retrieval occurs only after explicit run config and writer lease; venue/environment/account scope are bound; account receipts carry false capital/assisted flags; status exposes no credentials. Close refuses live native/reconciliation workers and clears its own credential/reader references.

Signed Binance reads are allowlisted/bounded; credential repr is protected; opening has a fixed TEST GATE; native dispatch handles cancellation/reduce-only exits/flatten/stop repair only and persists uncertainty without replay.
Bybit config binds DEMO/TESTNET; reader is GET-only and endpoint allowlisted; opening remains a fixed TEST GATE; protection readback requires exact current Full MarkPrice stop evidence.
Native node binds exact venue/account/product, captures a closed event type set, persists typed receipts with generic failure codes, and has bounded queues.
Native Bybit host is bounded and delegates OMS effects through the pinned adapter; receipts are typed/identity-bound and failures use fixed codes.
Run manifests require capital_enabled=false, assisted_enabled=false, holdout_access=false; demo OMS is an explicit separate child; desktop smoke starts no live run and carries false authority flags.

findings.qualification_boundary: The opened demo/test code is not evidence of supported live account operation or capital enablement. Exchange protection equivalence remains a TEST GATE.

findings.title: S41 modifies shared V1 journal and writer-lock code

evidence.observation: Changes add locking around journal wrappers/close; indexed bounded unresolved reads and client-order lookups; exact-idempotent economic-event writes; optional client-order filtering for execution evidence; capability qualification lookup.
Bootstrap adds four indexes with IF NOT EXISTS without changing the schema version.
The POSIX flock path is retained; a Windows byte-range lease sidecar is added and held for ownership lifetime.
The V1 economic-event duplicate test expectation changed from rejecting a duplicate to accepting exact replay.

findings.review_note: No direct safety-invariant regression was established by static inspection. These are shared V1 persistence/concurrency paths and require the coordinator's explicit V1 regression gate; this review did not run it.
required_review: Confirm exact duplicate economic receipts are byte/field-identical and conflicts still fail.
Exercise POSIX and Windows writer exclusion, cleanup, stale ownership, and restart behavior.
Run existing V1 journal, recovery, protection, no-reversal, and phase 0-6 regression suites against the final integrated SHA.

historical_audit_handling.usage_rule: These read-only audits describe code at the stated baseline SHA and are not current gap assertions. Revalidate each finding against the current source tree before using it in closure accounting.
